injuries.icd_description: Multiple superficial injuries of lower leg

manifestations.description: He now has no dossiflexion or plantar flexion in his left foot
the subtalar joint movement is reduced by 20%
Inversion is reduced by 30% with pain at the extremes and eversion is reduced by 30%, also with pain at the extremes.
He experiences pain at the ankle after a long walk.
If he gets up and starts to walk after having sat down for a long time, he will have a limp.
The skin over the right knee is 30% less efficient with scarring and keloid formation.
He used to play football but is no longer able to do so.
He has been assessed to have a 30% impairment of the left leg which is a 12% impairment of the whole man.
There is a chance of osteoarthritis and this will increase the disability to 15% in about 20 years time.

treatments_received: debridement and suturing of the wound (on the same day as admission)
open reduction and internal fixation of the ankle fracture using a plate and K-wire
further debridement and skin grafting (22nd April, 1988)
removal of the transfixing screw (29th May, 1988)
ankle joint fusion (24th August, 1989) (St. Theresa's Hospital)
treatments_future: anti-arthritis pain relief medication (likely as the years go by)
possible further operation for fusion of subtalar joint (40% likelihood in 20 years as opined by Dr. O'Donovan)

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He used to play football but is no longer able to do so.
No dorsiflexion or plantar flexion in left foot; reduced subtalar movement; reduced inversion and eversion with pain; difficulty in squatting; limp after sitting.
He is now unable to continue his previous work as a skilled carpenter and it is most unlikely that he can resume his previous work in future.
Scars at the medial aspect of the ankle joint, lateral aspect of the left leg, donor site of the left thigh and minor scars at the right knee with keloid formation.
